r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: All 7 close-criteria items reproduced/verified against source, not trusted from the report. (1) Position-sum EXACTNESS: compose_sector_predictions sums mu via plain float addition (line 179-181), test_position_sum_exact_via_nest_sectors asserts result.mu == expected_mu (bit-exact, no pytest.approx tolerance) using a REAL nest_sectors() mapping; test_misassignment_falsifies_position_sum independently reproduced by hand-tracing: moving segs[2] from sector 2 to sector 1 changes composed_wrong[2].mu by exactly -segs[2].mu and composed_wrong[1].mu changes too -- genuinely falsifies, not a tautology. (2) Student-t coverage: score_sector builds PredictiveT via src.common.student_t.predictive_t (confirmed: PredictiveT wraps scipy stats.t, not stats.norm); well-calibrated-vs-understated-sigma tests reproduced green myself (11/11 pass, see r3). (3) Consume-not-remint: grepped sector_scorecard.py for literal 0.90/0.85/0.50 -- zero matches; the only appearance is the import statement (lines 71-75) and test_frozen_triple_is_imported_not_reminted asserts identity (, not ) against frozen_constants' module-level objects. (4) Gate fires only on gross-miscalib: assert_not_grossly_miscalibrated (line 339-352) checks ONLY sizing.grossly_miscalibrated (coverage < GROSS_MISCALIB_BOUND=0.50); SECTOR_CALIB_COVERAGE_OBSERVED_MIN (0.85) only feeds meets_observed_min, never referenced in the raise condition. Reproduced test_gate_does_not_fire_above_gross_miscalib_bound (0.7 -> no raise) and test_gate_fires_below_gross_miscalib_bound (0.3 -> raises) both green. (5) No leakback: compose_sector_predictions signature (lines 127-132) has no official_time/official parameter at all -- confirmed by reading the signature directly, and the test's own inspect.signature assertion (line 257-258) is redundant-but-confirms. score_sector consumes official_time only to compute within_interval/residual/pit on an already-frozen (dataclass frozen=True) ComposedSector -- cannot mutate composed.mu/sigma. (6) n_eff combination: min(m.n_eff for m in members) (line 183) -- judged reasonable: lower n_eff -> smaller Student-t nu (fatter tail) AND larger epistemic scale inflation sqrt(1+1/n_eff) (student_t.py lines 218-224), so MIN is the CONSERVATIVE (widest-interval) choice among plausible per-segment n_eff, not an optimistic one -- sound and honestly documented (module docstring + implement-result). GAP noted: no test directly asserts composed.n_eff == min(members) or exercises coverage calibration through a MULTI-segment compose_sector_predictions call with heterogeneous n_eff -- the coverage tests (well-calibrated / understated-sigma) construct ComposedSector directly with a single fixed n_eff=30, bypassing the min-combination code path entirely. This is a real test-coverage gap on an executed-but-unasserted line, not a correctness defect -- flagged as a non-blocking observation, matching the handoff's own instruction to flag only if it materially distorts coverage (which I could not empirically test either way, but the analytic direction is conservative/safe). (7) pyright-0 + 11/11 tests reproduced myself on the pinned interpreter (see r3-evidence). Verdict: handoff satisfied within allowed scope, one non-blocking observation.
